prompt: Your first game plan, stage by stage. Put the steps in the order you carry them out from stage 2 to stage 4.

steps: Level to 7 at 4-1, then roll for the 2-star upgrades your board is missing
Buy pairs and field every 2-star you make; level to 5 at 2-5
Commit to one direction from 4-2 on: your augments, your items and the units you already have decide it
Level to 6 at 3-2 and combine your components into two items on the units you have
Save toward 50 gold through the rest of stage 3 while the board holds

explanation:
Stage 2 is about the board: buy pairs, turn them into 2-stars, put the 2-stars on the board, and take level 5 at 2-5 so the fifth unit fights. At 3-2 you level to 6 with the lobby and slam two completed items on the units you actually have; an item on the board wins fights now, a component on the bench wins nothing. The rest of stage 3 is the save: with a stable board you buy nothing and let interest take you to 50. At 4-1 you level to 7 and spend the bank rolling for the 2-star upgrades your carry and tank are missing. From 4-2 you commit: one direction, chosen from your augments, your items and the units you already have, and you stop saving for a plan that has not started.

The order matters because each step pays for the next. Skipping the save means arriving at 4-1 with nothing to roll. Rolling in stage 3 instead of saving is the same mistake. Committing before 4-2 locks you into whatever you had at 3-2, which is usually not much.
principle: Strongest board, then save, then level and roll at 4-1, then commit. In that order.
commonMistake: Rolling in stage 3 for upgrades and then having no bank for the level-7 rolldown at 4-1 where the upgrades actually appear.
hint: Work forwards from stage 2 and ask, for each step, what it costs and where the gold for it comes from.
